subject: Segregated runtime RFP — technical commitments and evidence
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@novahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: 2028-10-31T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: segregated runtime — technical commitments and clarifications

Connor,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is NovaHealth's technical questionnaire for segregated runtimes (RFP #NH-2028-77). We need concrete commitments and evidence for the items below in order to progress to procurement/tech review:

- Network isolation: VPC diagrams, egress controls, and proof of no public egress by default.
- Operator access and authentication model (e.g., operator vs customer keys).
- KMS/HSM integration, key owner separation, and key usage audit events.
- Patch and supply-chain controls: signed artifacts, SBOM, and update process for offline sites.
- Telemetry and log retention: what is collected, what leaves the environment, and retention windows.
- Timeline and artifacts you can provide (runbooks, operator checklists, KMS scope).

Can you provide a written response with attachments by EOD Nov 6? Also note this procurement requires evidence for a PCI-adjacent environment. If you have a quick separate checklist we can use to scope the security review that would be helpful.

Regards,
Alice Park
Procurement Manager, NovaHealth
alice.park@novahealth.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: segregated runtime — technical commitments and clarifications

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise commitment-level response; we will attach the referenced artifacts as separate files (see attachments list). If acceptable I propose a 30-minute technical review to walk NovaHealth's security team through the controls.

1) Network isolation
- Commitment: Redwood will deploy into a customer-dedicated VPC/subnet topology. Default egress is blocked; any allowed egress requires an explicit firewall policy and documented justification.
- Evidence: VPC topology diagram (segregated-runtime-architecture.pdf), sample iptables/ACL export.

2) Operator access & auth model
- Commitment: Operator access is role-based and time-limited; operators authenticate via customer-managed SSO (SAML/OIDC) when available. For on-prem/air-gapped installs we support operator accounts that require pre-provisioned SSH certificates and local operator vault encryption.
- Evidence: operator-runbook-v1.md (includes operator auth flow), list of operator roles and separation of duties.

3) KMS/HSM integration
- Commitment: We integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and provide support for HSM-backed keys in Private deployments. Key material never leaves HSM boundary. We support dual control for key rotations on request.
- Evidence: kms-key-scope-table.csv and redwood-compliance-headers.pdf showing audit events and KMS call traces.

4) Patch & supply-chain controls
- Commitment: All inbound artifacts for private installs are signed. We provide SBOMs for release images and a documented offline update process with signed payloads.
- Evidence: rfi-evidence-bundle.zip contains sample SBOM, signature verification steps, and update playbook.

5) Telemetry & log retention
- Commitment: No customer PII/PHI is exfiltrated by default. Telemetry can be configured to stay local; by default runtime health metrics are kept within the customer's environment and only aggregated anonymized metrics (if opted-in) are sent to Redwood. Retention windows are configurable; default operator logs retained 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Evidence: telemetry appendix included in attached PDF.

6) Timeline & deliverables
- We can provide the full evidence package and a walk-through by Nov 8. For installations, standard Private deployment SOW is 6–8 weeks from contract signature for a single-site installation; multi-site/air-gapped projects vary.

Next steps: I'll attach the artifacts here. Please confirm whether you prefer a technical walkthrough on Nov 8 (US morning) or Nov 9 (US afternoon) and whether you need an NDA/DocuSign before we share the full SBOM sample.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
Attachments: segregated-runtime-architecture.pdf (diagram), operator-runbook-v1.md (runbook), kms-key-scope-table.csv (KMS mapping), rfi-evidence-bundle.zip (sample SBOM & signatures)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: NovaHealth RFP follow-up — deliverable checklist

Connor / Naomi — quick internal note to lock down artifacts and ownership before the walkthrough: 

- I will finalize the VPC diagram and export a sanitized ACL/iptables snippet (non-prod).
- Naomi, can you prepare the SBOM sample and include the signature verification README in rfi-evidence-bundle.zip? Also add a short table that maps which fields in the SBOM are vendor-supplied vs build-time.
- Security will provide a redlined KMS usage matrix (kms-key-scope-table.csv) showing which keys are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed and the audit event names we emit.
- Ops: operator-runbook-v1.md will include step-by-step operator tasks for patching, emergency rollback, and vendor escalation contacts.

Target: have the full package uploaded to the Drive folder and a single zipped bundle by COB 2028-11-06. I will also prepare a two-page one-pager for procurement summarizing the commitments.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Alice Park <alice.park@novahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: segregated runtime — technical commitments and clarifications

Connor, Ben — thank you for the prompt and thorough response. This addresses most of our high-level questions. A couple of clarifications before the walkthrough: 

- For PCI-adjacent environments we need confirmation that any egress allowed by operator action is logged to a customer-controlled audit log and that the log is tamper-evident. Can you confirm the log forwarding and tamper-evidence approach?
- We will require a short statement of how key rotation events are provable (e.g., HSM event IDs or audit chain).

DocuSign/NDA: Procurement prefers an NDA in place before we exchange SBOM samples. I've attached our standard mutual NDA (link below) — can Redwood countersign? If so, we can move to the technical walkthrough.

Availability: Nov 8 at 10:00 AM PT works for our security engineers. Please send a calendar invite and preferred meeting platform.

Regards,
Alice Park
Procurement Manager, NovaHealth
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: segregated runtime — technical commitments and clarifications (Kickoff)

Hi Alice — confirmed. We countersigned the mutual NDA and uploaded the signed copy to the Drive link below. We will not share the SBOM sample until the NDA is in place; once countersigned you will see rfi-evidence-bundle.zip in the folder.

Meeting: Nov 8 at 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). Platform: Zoom (link in calendar).

Short answers to your remaining clarifications: 
- Egress logging and tamper-evidence: all operator-initiated egress actions generate an auditable event written to a WORM-style customer log sink (S3 with object lock or equivalent on-prem store). Events are signed with a server-side key and a chain-of-custody header; we provide the verification script included in rfi-evidence-bundle.zip.
- Key rotation provability: HSM rotation events produce immutable audit IDs; we surface the HSM event id and a signed rotation certificate. Example event ids are in kms-key-scope-table.csv.

Artifacts are uploaded here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleRunbook. DocuSign countersign URL: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/NH-RFP-77-NDA (completed).

Looking forward to the walkthrough. Connor

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
Attachments (uploaded): segregated-runtime-architecture.pdf, operator-runbook-v1.md, kms-key-scope-table.csv, rfi-evidence-bundle.zip
